relations.subject: Dietmar Otto Ernst Rothermund
relations.role: professor of the history of South Asia
relations.evidence: Dietmar Otto Ernst Rothermund (20 January 1933 in Kassel –  9 March 2020 in Dossenheim) was a German historian and professor of the history of South Asia at the Ruprecht-Karls University in Heidelberg.

relations.subject: Dietmar Otto Ernst Rothermund
relations.evidence: With the help of a Fulbright scholarship, he was able to study in Pennsylvania and write his dissertation there at the age of 26, entitled: The Layman's Progress.

relations.subject: Dietmar Otto Ernst Rothermund
relations.role: research assistant to the Chair of History
relations.evidence: In 1963 Rothermund became a research assistant to the Chair of History at the South Asia Institute in Heidelberg.

relations.subject: Dietmar Otto Ernst Rothermund
relations.role: Chair of the History of South Asia
relations.evidence: Shortly after his habilitation The Land and the Law in India, 1875-1900, in 1968, he was appointed Chair of the History of South Asia at the South Asia Institute.

relations.subject: Dietmar Otto Ernst Rothermund
relations.evidence: Shortly after his stay in India, Rothermund visited the National University of Australia as a visiting fellow in 1963.

relations.subject: Dietmar Otto Ernst Rothermund
relations.evidence: With History of India, Rothermund, together with his colleague Hermann Kulke, created standard work, which has been translated into Italian, Turkish, Romanian and Chinese.

relations.subject: Werner Conze
relations.evidence: Almost his entire academic career took place at the then still young South Asia Institute, which had just been founded by Werner Conze.

relations.subject: Dietmar Otto Ernst Rothermund
relations.object: European Association of South Asian Studies
relations.evidence: With Rothermund as its founding father and long-time chairman (1997-2006), EASAS developed into one of the most important European associations of its kind.
